meta_reflection: A zero-experiment milestone is a process signal, not a research signal — it means the outer loop (conductor + planner) failed to produce runnable work within the milestone window. The retrospective for such a milestone should focus entirely on diagnosing the activation gap rather than analyzing experiment-level performance. Future milestones should treat a zero-experiment retro as a P0 process incident: root-cause the stall, apply the fix within the same session, and confirm the next milestone activates at least one experiment before the outer loop moves on.
